parameters.content:
## Setup checklist
1. Reuses the same "Chatwoot API" httpHeaderAuth credential the whizz-get-conversation-messages workflow already has configured — no new credential needed if that one's set up.
2. Whizz calls this at POST https://n8n.aiingo.com/webhook/whizz-send-conversation-message with body {id, content, replyToId?} (id = the Chatwoot conversation id, replyToId = optional id of the message being quote-replied to) and expects back the created message: {id, content, message_type, created_at, status, sender_type} on success, or {error} on failure.
3. This sends a free-text outgoing message. WhatsApp's own 24-hour customer-service-window rule still applies — Chatwoot will reject the send with an error if the window has closed, which this workflow passes straight back as {error} rather than trying to work around it (the frontend checks the window itself before showing the composer, but this is the real enforcement point).
4. replyToId maps to Chatwoot's content_attributes.in_reply_to — not verified against a live send from this account; if Chatwoot rejects or ignores it, check the exact field name in Chatwoot's current API docs and adjust the jsonBody below.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ content: $json.body.content, message_type: 'outgoing', private: false, ...($json.body.replyToId ? { content_attributes: { in_reply_to: $json.body.replyToId } } : {}) }) }}
